head: f1b2489f5b1c929e81eeae79a469b2b27c47e340
title: Record bench lanes B16, B16b and B16c: Direction B's B0 graded, and B-CRF and B-AAF graded at the path's floor (#629)

selected_body_lines.text: - The second run's tap covered the bind. 99.6 ms after the unbind command, the peer sent PROBE_TX (IEEE 1722.1's CONNECT_TX) for its own talker onto the network, and again 200 ms later. Nothing answered in the rest of the capture, 49.6 s, so the stream never started.

Direction B's bench quality metric is now graded for both followed sources, B-CRF and B-AAF, and with the DUT on INTERNAL. Lane B6's timed ratio for B-CRF and B-AAF was not run. Direction B's INTERNAL mismatch control did not run: B0 had the peer following the DUT, and the exception covers B-CRF and B-AAF only. #645 stays open, so #629 stays open.

- the earlier probes give round 8's exit statuses, verdicts and named lines (their summary counts and the check's hash follow the new page and check), but for R624-7's `footnote_ref_and` form: its footnote definition, appended after the page's last line, is named at line 4426 instead of 4274, because the page grew;

- R624-9-R1 is applied above: earlier probes retained exit statuses, verdicts and named lines, with the stated footnote movement; their full output bytes also contain updated counts and the check's hash. R625-9's manager-applied corrections remain: “99.6 ms after the unbind command” and “line 4426”.

decisions.body:
[A10] **Decision on the two changed control expectations (R625-8-F1, [6132288182](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/725#issuecomment-6132288182)).** Round 8 moved the check to the pinned parser's visible text ([6130721355](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/629#issuecomment-6130721355)). Two frozen diagnostics from earlier rounds now read differently. Both are accepted as the correct results under that contract.

1. **Round 4's link-label control** (`in [37](#b16c-attribution) blocks`). The reader sees "37 blocks", so the digit is now a measurement that only a row may claim, where round 4 expected UNCOVERED but not a measurement. This supersedes round 4's expectation and the inherited copies in the round 5, 6 and 7 runners.
2. **Round 7's comment inside a code span** (`` `CLOCK_DOMAIN 7<!-- -->ppm` ``). Inside a code span the parser presents the text verbatim as visible code, so no HTML comment exists to refuse. The digit is now UNCOVERED at its line, where round 7 expected MARKUP. This supersedes round 7's expectation.

Both altered pages are still refused (exit 1), with the number named at the correct source line and both receipts written. That remains the frozen requirement. The historical runners keep their recorded outcomes: 7/8, 21/22, 38/39 and 48/50, each failing only on these superseded expectations. They are not reported as wholly green. The round 8 runner (73/73) is the standing set.

[A10] **R625-9 applied to the PR body.** The head is unchanged at `cb5ff79f`.
- R625-9-F1: "99.6 ms after the bind command" now reads "99.6 ms after the unbind command". The tap records DISCONNECT_RX at 2.600600 s and the first CONNECT_TX at 2.700216 s; the findings already use that origin.
- R625-9-R1: the locator now reads line 4426.

No source or page change was needed. The next delta review confirms the body.

[A10] **B16 findings, round 10 (documents only, no bench work).** R624-9 is NEGATIVE ([6134093761](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/725#issuecomment-6134093761)). The pinned cmark-gfm reports a bare e-mail autolink, its text and the text after it with no position at all, so the check drops them silently: `x@example.com 7 ppm` escapes. R625-9's finding and its residue were applied to the PR body (6133971231). This is the third round in which the parser's own reporting hides text from the check. The class is closed by conservation, not by enumerating node kinds. Executor [A603].

1. **No node without a position.** Any node the check reads or judges, other than a soft or hard break, that has no valid source start refuses its whole block. The refusal is named at the first covered line the block reaches. This covers the e-mail and `mailto:` autolinks and any other zero-position kind.
2. **Digit conservation.** For each covered block, render it with the pinned renderer, the same one round 8 uses, and take its visible text. The multiset of digits in that visible text must equal the multiset of digits the check judged for the block. Any difference refuses the block, named at its first covered line. This catches any node kind the parser misplaces or omits, whether or not it is known today.
3. **Controls.** R624-9's `probe_r624_9_autolink.py`, unchanged: every `detect` case exits 1, naming its 7 at the true line (19 or `README.md:15`) or refused there. The unchanged page passes. Add a standing control per autolink form, and one where a later line's figure in a paragraph must be named at its own line, not the paragraph's first (R624-9's 2301-for-2302 case). Add the zero-position kinds to the parser-extents audit. Every earlier runner and probe keeps its outcome.
4. **Texts.** The page, the index row and the PR body state the rule. Apply R624-9-R1. The location paragraph gains round 9 at `author-r9/` (`4ab00ba5`).

Post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.
